# Source 122 — NIST: AI Congressional Mandates, Executive Orders and Actions

- **URL:** https://www.nist.gov/artificial-intelligence/ai-congressional-mandates-executive-orders-and-actions
- **Publisher:** National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
- **Published:** page created 2025-01-21, **updated 2026-03-27**
- **Type:** Official agency reference page (NIST AI program)
- **Status:** fetched 2026-09-14 (full text, http 200)

## Key claims (as stated in source)
- NIST's AI efforts are driven by congressional mandates, Presidential EOs/policies, industry and research-community needs, and NIST's own capabilities.
- **Chips and Science Act of 2022 (P.L. 117-167, 8/9/2022):** directs NIST to continue supporting AI/data science (carrying out the National AI Initiative Act of 2020), improve AI-enabled cybersecurity, establish testbeds for robust/trustworthy AI/ML, expand AI capabilities, support AI chip/hardware measurement R&D, develop technical standards for safe/trustworthy AI, create a risk-management framework, and develop cybersecurity tools/encryption/best practices.
- **National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 (P.L. 116-283, 1/1/2021):** directs NIST to advance collaborative frameworks/standards/guidelines for AI, develop a risk-mitigation framework, support bias-testing standards, and conduct stakeholder outreach; established the **National AI Advisory Committee (NAIAC)** and a **National AI Research Resource (NAIRR) Task Force**.
- **Executive Orders related to NIST AI work:**
  - **"Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan" (7/23/2025):** NIST named in many recommended actions (frontier AI protecting free speech; open-source/open-weight AI; AI adoption; AI-enabled science; interpretability/control/robustness; AI evaluations ecosystem; high-security data centers; critical-infrastructure cybersecurity; secure-by-design AI; federal AI incident response; biosecurity; national-security risk evaluation of frontier models).
  - **EO 14179 "Removing Barriers to American Leadership in AI" (1/23/2025):** action plan to sustain US AI dominance; review of actions under EO 14110.
  - **EO on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI (10/30/2023) [Rescinded 1/20/2025]:** directed NIST to develop guidelines/reports on Generative AI, secure software development, synthetic content, global standards engagement, and testing environments.
  - **EO on Promoting the Use of Trustworthy AI in the Federal Government (12/3/2020):** established federal AI principles reflected in the **NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)**.
  - **EO on Maintaining American Leadership in AI (2/14/2019):** directed NIST to create a plan for federal engagement in AI technical standards.

## Verification notes
- Consistent with draft.md usage (NIST AI RMF as voluntary framework driven by congressional mandates/EOs).
- Primary official NIST page — authoritative.
- Note: the NIST AI RMF is a **voluntary** framework (the draft describes it as voluntary); this page confirms it stems from the 2020 EO + National AI Initiative Act, not a binding statute.
